newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf Air owners agree on loan for troubled carrier.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air owners agree on loan for troubled carrier.

text.p: The owners of Gulf Air have agreed to grant the debt-ridden regional carrier an interest-free loan to help it overcome financial difficulties, the airline's chairman said on Sunday.

The owners -- the governments of Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and Abu Dhabi emirate in the United Arab Emirates -- were also studying raising the company's capital, said Qatar's Minister of Communications and Transport Sheikh Ahmed bin Nasser al-Thani, who currently holds the rotating seat of chairman.
The loan was sanctioned at a meeting of the Gulf Air board in the Qatari capital on Saturday, he said.
"All four owners were in agreement and the amount given is the same as requested by Gulf Air," he told reporters, but did not disclose the figure.
"Details will be revealed within the next two weeks by the company's financial section," he said.

Earlier this year, reports said the loss-making airline had asked for 100 million Bahraini dinars ($265.3 million) in fresh capital to increase its resources and avert a potential default on debts -- estimated at close to $2 billion.
Gulf Air, currently capitalised at 250 million Bahraini dinars ($657 million), is equally owned by the four partners.

It was not immediately clear whether all four would contribute to the loan equally or whether Abu Dhabi and Bahrain -- which have the lion's share of Gulf Air's facilities and infrastructure on their soil -- would chip in more than others.
In 1995, Gulf Air's net losses amounted to $159 million, the worst since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis when the company suffered a deficit of $100 million.
The airline has embarked on a drastic structural review, including a staff cutback, closure of uneconomic routes and the leasing of aircraft to reduce the losses.

"The future looks encouraging ... in 1996 that sum (the loss) had been reduced to $30 million, and the figures which they (Gulf Air) have shown us indicate that by the end of this year, the deficit will stand at $12 million," Sheikh Ahmed said.
He said the owner-states had ..."every confidence in the airline's future and would do everything necessary to bail it out from the present difficulty".
